pr_title: Fix crash for invalid Content-Type in ShowExceptions middleware
pr_body:

issue_context.title: It is not possible to handle "not a valid MIME type" error using the exceptions_app = self.routes when the value of CONTENT_TYPE header is invalid
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

almost same as
https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/43094

1. Generate a new application:

```
rails new InvalidMimeTypeApp --skip-action-mailer --skip-action-mailbox --skip-action-text --skip-active-storage --skip-action-cable --skip-sprockets --skip-spring --skip-listen --skip-javascript --skip-turbolinks --skip-jbuilder --skip-test --skip-system-test --skip-bootsnap

index 09705d1..1b28aee 100644
--- a/app/controllers/application_controller.rb
+++ b/app/controllers/application_controller.rb
@@ -1,2 +1,13 @@

+    def about
+        render '/about'
+    end
+
+    def not_found
+        render json: { error: "some error message" }, status: :not_found
+    end
+    
+    def unsupported
+        render json: { error: "some error message" }, status: :unsupported_media_type
+    end
 end

index e28b261..d960e3c 100644

+++ b/config/application.rb
@@ -38,5 +38,7 @@ module InvalidMimeTypeApp

   end
 end

@@ -7,4 +7,8 @@ Rails.application.routes.draw do

+
+  get "/about", to: "application#about"

+  match "/415", to: "application#unsupported", via: :all

```

3. Run the server and cURL the application with an invalid request:

```
 curl -i -X POST -H "Content-Type: invalid;" http://localhost:3000/about
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
x-request-id: 122a50df-16d0-465a-97d6-f0dc4b7bed85
x-runtime: 0.004729
server-timing: 
Content-Length: 182

500 Internal Server Error
If you are the administrator of this website, then please read this web application's log file and/or the web server's log file to find out what went wrong.%                                                                                                                                                         (base) 
```

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->

The application calls the `ApplicationController#not_found` or `ApplicationController#unsupported` action as stated in the `config/routes.rb` file.

This PR can fix the behavior but I don't know why this PR was not merged.
https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/46757

Since the `ActionController::RoutingError (No route matches [POST] "/about"):` error occurs first, a 404 error would be sufficient for my use, but it may be more appropriate to have a 415 error drawn.

review_comments: I'm not sure this is the right fix. Why is the `CONTENT_TYPE` being set to `text/html`? That's almost certainly not the correct type for request parameters.

~~Probably not, yes. But any other type that is more likely to be correct like application/json or form data will also only be correct by chance. The client already sent bogus data.~~

~~I went with symetry with `HTTP_ACCEPT`, however I have no problems with using something like `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` instead.~~
This is the the content type of the error page we want rendered. The request parameters aren't sent to the error page.

Isn't that what the existing `HTTP_ACCEPT` header controls?

The backtrace in the linked issue is coming from `ParamWrapper#_wrapper_enabled?`, and if the exception is rescued in that method then a second error is raised when the exceptions app tries to call `filtered_parameters` (because its unable to parse the invalid `CONTENT_TYPE` of the request params)

HTTP_ACCEPT doesn't control the CONTENT_TYPE. The problem of the issue isn't that the exception is raised on `_wrapper_enabled?` but that the exceptions application also raises an error in the same place. If the content-type is made valid it would not and the correct exception page would be rendered.
